title: AI 2041: ten visions of the future
text:
I listened to this as an audiobook AI 2041: Ten Visions for Our Future (2021). It was written in 2021 at the end of the Covid pandemic and just before ChatGPT was released, so a lifetime ago in terms of AI developments. However, the book is outstanding in its framing of real-world fictional scenarios and the discussion that follows.

AI 2041: Ten Visions for Our Future (2021) pairs Kai-Fu Lee (AI researcher, former president of Google China) with Chen Qiufan (acclaimed Chinese sci-fi novelist). The structure is unusual: each of the ten chapters opens with a short story set in 2041, written by Qiufan, depicting how a specific AI technology has reshaped daily life somewhere in the world — followed by a nonfiction essay from Lee that explains the real technology behind the story and forecasts how it's likely to develop over the next two decades. 

Each chapter pairs a story situated in 2041 by Chen Qiufan with an analytical essay by Kai-Fu Lee covering the present state of the technology and expectations for its development by 2041. The goal is to make abstract AI concepts (deep learning, GANs, quantum computing, AGI, etc.) tangible through narrative, while keeping the technical grounding rigorous. The book is generally optimistic about AI's potential to generate abundance, but doesn't shy away from risks like bias, job displacement, deepfakes, and autonomous weapons.

The Ten Visions, in Order

The Golden Elephant (India) — A deep-learning insurance/finance system makes decisions for a family that end up reinforcing caste and social biases, illustrating how data-driven optimization can entrench discrimination. Tech focus: deep learning, big data, AI bias/externalities.

Gods Behind the Masks (Nigeria) — A young programmer is pressured into producing a deepfake video meant to discredit a masked political movement, then has to find a way out of the scheme. Tech focus: computer vision, GANs, deepfakes, AI security.

Twin Sparrows (Seoul, South Korea) — Orphaned twin boys at an academy each design their own AI tutor/companion; one thrives under a gamified AI coach while the other (on the autism spectrum) flourishes with a gentler, creative AI guide — raising questions about over-optimized, achievement-obsessed parenting. Tech focus: natural language processing, GPT-style models, AI in education.

Contactless Love (Shanghai) — In a world still shaped by recurring COVID variants, a woman traumatized by the pandemic relies on robotic caregiving to manage daily life while struggling to reconnect with other humans. Tech focus: AI healthcare, robotics, pandemic-driven automation.

My Haunting Idol (Tokyo) — A devoted fan immerses himself in a virtual/AR recreation of a celebrity idol, exploring the seductive and potentially unhealthy pull of synthetic intimacy. Tech focus: VR/AR/mixed reality, brain-computer interfaces.

The Holy Driver (Munich) — Full vehicle autonomy collides with human trust, religion, and the role of people as mere "backups" to self-driving systems. Tech focus: autonomous vehicles, smart cities, ethics of automation.

Quantum Genocide (Munich/global) — A rogue quantum computing scientist plots revenge by threatening to break global encryption (including Bitcoin), nearly triggering catastrophe. Tech focus: quantum computing, cryptographic security, autonomous weapons/existential risk.

The Job Savior (San Francisco) — As automation displaces workers, a new "job reallocation" industry emerges to help people retrain and find new purpose. Tech focus: AI-driven job displacement, universal basic income debates.

Isle of Happiness — A society attempts to algorithmically measure and optimize human happiness itself, prompting philosophical questions about whether fulfillment can—or should—be quantified. Tech focus: AI and wellbeing metrics, the limits of optimization.

Dreaming of Plenitude (Mumbai) — A closing, more utopian vision of a post-scarcity world, where AI-optimized renewable energy (solar, wind, storage) drives costs toward zero and reshapes manufacturing and poverty itself. Tech focus: post-scarcity economics, clean energy + AI synergy.

A useful framing: the book moves roughly from individual/social harms (bias, deepfakes, education pressure) through technological risk (autonomy, quantum threats) to economic disruption and, finally, a more hopeful long-term vision — ending deliberately on abundance rather than dystopia.
